observations.statement: The core defines six complete Browser preview and visible testing surface controls, each with an explicit UI command identifier and handler location.

The two screenshot-selection commands expect browser.context_captured and runtime_artifact.created; add-selection expects only browser.context_captured; detach expects browser.session.state_changed; focus expects no domain event; keep-closed expects browser.session.closed.
Every command is required to be registered in the UICommand dispatcher with typed arguments and a result contract.
Every command names separate projected paths for availability and disabled-reason state before dispatch.
Event-producing commands require a correlated dispatch receipt, and their effect assertions prohibit fabricating command_applied events.

The accessibility contract requires stable role/name/description semantics, keyboard reachability and activation where visible, visible-focus preservation with deterministic return after dispatch or error, and assistive-technology exposure of the disabled reason.
Focus-browser-tab is explicitly modeled as layout/UI-only state: it records a no-persist dispatch receipt and emits no browser/runtime domain event.
Production certification explicitly requires render/control, dispatcher, typed-contract, state-projection, disabled-reason, receipt/event, accessibility, and regression evidence.
Event tests require command_id, origin, correlation_id, receipt linkage, and browser_session_id conditionally where applicable.
The observable event distinction between adding a selection and adding either screenshot selection is the presence of runtime_artifact.created for the screenshot commands.

candidate_findings.title: Typed command contracts have no exact schema
candidate_findings.statement: Each of the six records requires typed args/results or a typed payload/result contract, but the records define no argument fields, result variants, field types, validation rules, or error variants.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can produce mutually incompatible dispatcher payloads and results while satisfying the stated registration and fixture prose, so type and validation certification lacks a unique oracle.

candidate_findings.title: Screenshot variants are not discriminated by their observable contracts
candidate_findings.statement: The full-selection-screenshot and selection-screenshot commands have identical expected event types and materially identical event assertions; neither assertion identifies artifact kind, capture bounds, full-selection semantics, or another discriminator.
candidate_findings.impact: An implementation can produce the wrong screenshot variant yet still pass the named event tests, leaving capability correctness to consequential builder discretion.

candidate_findings.title: Dual-event screenshot effects lack ordering and partial-failure semantics
candidate_findings.statement: Each screenshot-selection command requires browser.context_captured and runtime_artifact.created, but the core does not specify event ordering, atomicity, partial-failure disposition, or when the receipt becomes durable relative to the two events.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can disagree on whether a context event may survive artifact-creation failure or whether retries duplicate one effect, producing inconsistent observable histories.

candidate_findings.title: Availability projections lack an exact state model
candidate_findings.statement: The core names availability and disabled-reason paths for all six commands but does not define availability values, enablement predicates, update triggers, freshness rules, or consistency between the two projections.
candidate_findings.impact: Controls can enable, disable, or announce reasons differently under the same browser state, and the state-projection tests cannot adjudicate the correct transition behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Session lifecycle events omit transition semantics
candidate_findings.statement: Detach-browser-tab identifies only browser.session.state_changed and keep-closed identifies only browser.session.closed; neither record defines source state, target state, preconditions, invalid-state behavior, or repeated-command idempotency.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders may implement incompatible session transitions or duplicate close effects while still emitting the required event name.

candidate_findings.title: Focus command receipt oracle is internally inconsistent
candidate_findings.statement: The focus effect contract and event-test requirement mandate a no-persist dispatch receipt, while the receipt-or-event assertion permits a no-persist command receipt or a route/open disposition.
candidate_findings.impact: Certification can accept an implementation without the receipt that the effect contract and event test require, weakening traceability and producing contradictory pass criteria.

candidate_findings.title: Accessibility behavior is descriptive rather than exact
candidate_findings.statement: The accessibility contract requires a stable role/name/description, keyboard activation where visible, and deterministic focus return, but it does not state the actual role, accessible name or description, activation gesture, visibility predicate, or focus-return target.
candidate_findings.impact: Different controls can all claim compliance while exposing different semantics and focus behavior, so the regression evidence lacks a unique accessibility oracle.

candidate_findings.title: Conditional browser session correlation is undefined
candidate_findings.statement: Every event-test requirement conditions browser_session_id on the phrase where applicable, but no applicability rule is given for any event or command in the core.
candidate_findings.impact: Producers may omit browser_session_id in different circumstances, undermining cross-event and receipt correlation for the same browser operation.

candidate_findings.title: Operational failure and repetition behavior is unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The side-effecting records define success events and correlated receipts but do not define cancellation, timeout, retry, deduplication, concurrency, or command-failure result behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Retries or concurrent dispatches can duplicate artifacts, context captures, state changes, or closure effects, and failures can be reported inconsistently.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Command routing authority is explicit at this layer: each UI command is paired with a named handlers::browser target.
The event-bearing commands explicitly identify expected domain-event names and require correlated receipt evidence without fabricated command_applied events.
The focus command has an explicit persistence disposition: no persisted browser/runtime domain event and a no-persist receipt.
Disabled-state GUI truth is explicitly projected from a named disabled-reason path and required to be surfaced to assistive technology.
The core provides named certification evidence categories rather than relying only on an unqualified implementation claim.

unknowns.statement: The consumers, retention behavior, and authority boundaries for browser.context_captured, runtime_artifact.created, browser.session.state_changed, browser.session.closed, and dispatch receipts are not identified within this core.
Whether Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md supplies the omitted payload schemas, event semantics, state transitions, or failure rules cannot be determined from this window.
The concrete availability values and user-visible disabled-reason copy cannot be determined from the named projection paths.
The runtime behavior on handler error, cancellation, timeout, retry, or concurrent duplicate dispatch cannot be determined from the success-oriented effect and evidence statements.
The cases in which browser_session_id is applicable cannot be determined from the conditional event-test wording.
